findings.title: Malformed judge block failure mode claims a test in T8 that T8 does not contain
findings.description: The Coverage Check section states "malformed judge block (inherited from `resolve_thresholds`, exercised in T8)," and the slice design's Failure Modes table (line 242) lists this as a distinct boundary with an explicit test column: "malformed judge block → flagged, not silently defaulted." However, T8's checklist contains no malformed-judge-block test case. T8 covers parametrized direction bands, floor-gated loosening, non-floor-gated tightening, unversioned refusal, and `read_current_thresholds` for registered/unregistered templates — but not a template whose `judge:` block has a non-numeric floor value. A junior AI following T8's checklist will not write this test, yet the coverage check gives false assurance that it is covered. Fix: add a checklist item to T8 such as "malformed `judge:` block (non-numeric `pass_floor`) → `read_current_thresholds` flags the template with a WARNING and falls back to `resolve_thresholds`' documented merge, never silently defaults."

findings.title: Lapsed-graduation signal mechanism is deferred to the implementer
findings.description: T13 states the lapsed-graduation case must be "distinguishable from 'config not yet due for sampling' at the CLI layer" but leaves the mechanism open: "return enough information (or have the CLI re-derive it via `find_graduation` against current results)." T14 mirrors this flexibility: "assert on whatever signal T13 produces for this — a return-value field, a paired lookup, or a logged WARNING." While the success criterion (lapse distinguishable from exhausted) is clear, the exact return-type shape is unspecified, which risks T13 and T14 being implemented by different agents with incompatible contract assumptions. Not blocking — the success criterion is testable either way — but pinning the signal (e.g., a `lapsed: list[GraduatedConfig]` return field or a documented side-channel) before implementation would prevent a cross-task integration mismatch.
